current.title: The Octopus Has 9 Brains. Here's Where They Are.
current.hook: Most of its brain isn't even in its head.
current.closing: Data counted his own brains. Still just the one.
current.question: Would you want a second brain in each arm? Tell me below.

segments.topic: where most of an octopus's neurons actually are
segments.say: An octopus runs on about 500 million neurons -- but only 180 million of them sit in its central brain. The other 320 million are out in its arms.

segments.topic: how many independent sensors an octopus's arms have
segments.say: That's because every one of its 280 suckers per arm is its own touch-and-taste sensor -- 2,240 of them across all eight arms, each wired straight into that arm's own nerves.

segments.topic: why a severed octopus arm keeps reacting
segments.say: And that control is so independent, a severed arm keeps reacting to touch and pain for up to 3,600 seconds after it's cut off -- a full hour, with no brain attached at all.

judge.one_line: A three-fact octopus story told mostly with stock bars and scales, with overlapping and edge-clipped labels and a mascot who perches instead of causing anything.
problems: The hook (hook@0.3 to hook@2.2) is a slow balance scale with small blocks and no octopus. Nothing in the first two seconds gives a reason to stay.
Data is clipped by the left frame edge and covers the '3' of '320M' throughout seg0.
In seg2:end the labels 'Suckers on one arm' and 'Suckers across all 8 arms 2,240' are printed on top of each other, and a stray cyan ellipse floats in seg2:mid.
seg2 and seg3 fall back to plain bar charts, and seg3 never says that 3,600 is seconds or what the '1' measures.
In seg3 Data just stands on top of the growing bar and does nothing.
In seg4 the label 'How long a severed arm keeps reacting' is cut off at both frame edges, and Data overlaps the label text at seg4:end.
fixes: Open on an octopus whose arms light up with neurons while the head stays dim, so the 320M vs 180M split is visible in frame 1.
Keep Data inside the safe area and away from value labels.

Rebuild seg2 as arms covered in suckers multiplying from 280 on one arm to 2,240 across eight, with Data lighting them up. Use one measured, non-overlapping label per value and remove the stray ellipse.
Rebuild seg3 as a severed arm twitching beside a clock that Data winds forward to a full hour, with the units on screen.
Fit the seg4 label inside the frame (wrap or shrink it to measured width) and keep Data off the text.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'.
